What changes around the open documents: a header on disk, a file that
appears and goes, the project's configuration, and the settings an editor
has for a folder without one.

-- lib/dgdtools.yml --
root: .
driver_config: ../mud.dgd
-- lib/mud.dgd --
include_dirs = ({ "/include" });
-- mud.dgd --
include_dirs = ({ "/include" });
-- lib/include/paths.h --
#define STORE "/obj/store"
-- lib/obj/store.c --
void put(string what) {}
-- lib/obj/a.c --
#include <paths.h>
void f() { STORE->put("x", 1); "/obj/chest"->open(); }
-- wizard/b.c --
void g() { "/players/ann/c"->nofn(); }
-- wizard/c.c --
void fn() {}
-- script --
settings wizard {"libPath": "/players/ann"}
initialize lib wizard
received workspace/configuration
open lib/obj/a.c
diagnostics lib/obj/a.c
# The patterns, and the one file the project is configured by that they
# do not reach: the driver's configuration, beside the lib.
received client/registerCapability
received window/logMessage

# The header changes on disk: STORE is another object.
write lib/include/paths.h "#define STORE \"/obj/nowhere\"\n"
watched changed lib/include/paths.h
diagnostics lib/obj/a.c
# A file appears.
write lib/obj/chest.c "void open() {}\n"
watched created lib/obj/chest.c
diagnostics lib/obj/a.c
# The configuration changes: a rule is turned off, and the driver's
# configuration is the one in the lib.
write lib/dgdtools.yml "root: .\ndriver_config: mud.dgd\nlint:\n  rules:\n    target-object-missing: off\n"
watched changed lib/dgdtools.yml
diagnostics lib/obj/a.c
# The one beside the lib is no longer read, and the one in the lib is not
# under the patterns: the watchers are registered again for it.
received client/unregisterCapability
received client/registerCapability

# A folder without a config file, and what the settings say of it.
open wizard/b.c
diagnostics wizard/b.c
received window/logMessage
settings wizard {}
configuration
diagnostics wizard/b.c
shutdown
exit
